question: A trader marks an item 40% above its cost price and gives a discount of 10%. Find his profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let CP = 100

MP = 140

After 10% discount ⇒ SP = 140 × 0.9 = 126

Profit = 126 − 100 = 26

Profit% = 26%

**∴ Answer = 26%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup = 40%, Discount = 10%

**Formula used:**

MP = CP × (1 + markup)

SP = MP × (1 − discount)

Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = 100

⇒ MP = 100 × 1.40 = 140

⇒ SP = 140 × 0.90 = 126

⇒ Profit = 126 − 100 = 26

⇒ Profit% = (26 ÷ 100) × 100 = 26%

**∴ The correct answer is 26%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage

Apply markup and discount multiplicatively

Shortcut Tip

Assume CP = 100 for quick calculations

Profit Concept

Profit is always calculated on CP

Key Insight

Net effect = (1 + markup)(1 − discount)
